transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-29
Start time: 10:30 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Lena Ortiz (Redwood AE), Marcus Ng (Redwood SE), Priya Shah (Datafoundry Head of Platform), Ethan Cole (SRE), Marta Ruiz (Security), Sam (Dev)

Summary (auto): weekly pilot check-in for Redwood Private VPC pilot. Focus on networking test results, routing fallback behavior, and plan to upgrade runtime to address high tail latency seen in long sequences.

[00:00] Lena (Redwood): hey everyone thanks for joining, we'll keep this tight — Marcus and I will run through the results, then open Q&A and next steps.
[00:18] Priya (Datafoundry): thanks, appreciate it — we've got Ethan and Marta on for the sec and infra bits. Sam might jump in on the network traces.
[00:35] Marcus (Redwood): ok quick recap: last week we saw elevated p95 on requests over 2k tokens in your staging region, looks correlated with cold kv-cache misses and occasional cross-az routing. We pushed a small patch to routing rules and gathered new traces.
[01:05] Ethan (Datafoundry): yes that p95 spike was reproducible, but odd — sometimes the traffic goes to a different pod in the other AZ and that adds the extra RTT. We ran 1000 requests, 10% showed +120ms tail.
[01:42] Marcus (Redwood): right — two root causes: 1) our smart routing was falling back to a lower-capacity pool when capacity tests hit a spike, 2) in your VPC peering setup the ephemeral ENI route table had a slightly different priority so occasional packets took a longer path.
[02:12] Marta (Security): quick question on data plane — is the KV cache encrypted-at-rest in the on-prem variant? we need to confirm KMS/HSM usage.
[02:30] Lena (Redwood): yes both at-rest and in-flight encryption — we'll send the KMS integration diagram. note that for Private there is an option to bring your own KMS.
[02:48] Priya: perfect, we'll need that for our audit.
[03:05] Marcus: jumping back to the traces — Sam, did you upload the traceroute and iptables dump you mentioned?
[03:18] Sam (Dev): uploaded to the shared folder, link in the meeting notes, though the file names got truncated in our system so sorry if it's hard to parse.
[03:35] Marcus: got it — I pulled it, looks like some NATting behavior in the AZ-b region; that explains the transient routing.
[04:00] (crosstalk)
[04:12] Priya: is the fallback policy configurable per-route? we don't want lot of cross-az failovers during peak.
[04:25] Marcus: yes we expose routing policies — you can prefer same-AZ, or prefer low-cost pools, or aggressive fallback for reliability. Right now pilot uses the default of cost-balanced with soft failover. We can change to same-AZ-preferred for your staging region to see if it stabilizes p95.
[04:58] Ethan: that'd be good, what's the tradeoff? more cost or capacity headroom needed?
[05:10] Marcus: same-AZ preference reduces cross-az traffic but might cause slightly higher rejections during localized spikes; however the KV cache TTL and better batching can offset that. We also have a runtime patch 0.9.3 that improves concurrent kv-cache lookups and reduces lock contention.
[05:36] Priya: runtime 0.9.3 — how risky is that? can we canary it?
[05:48] Lena: absolutely canary. Marcus will open the support ticket; we recommend staging canary first with 2 pods, ramp to 20% traffic, then full roll. We'll share the suggested rollout plan.
[06:12] Marcus: the upgrade includes a small kernel optimization and a config change to batching defaults; we measured ~8-12% lower p95 in our internal lab for sequences >2k. But we need to run your workload to confirm.
[06:40] Sam: any breaking config changes? we run a custom NLB and a few iptables rules.
[06:50] Marcus: no breaking API changes, but there is an expect config flag for kv-cache sizing that may default differently. We'll include a migration checklist.
[07:08] Marta: back to security — audit logs format, retention, and export. We've asked about whether logs are forwarded to our SIEM via syslog or S3.
[07:22] Lena: both are supported; Private can stream logs to your S3 bucket or to your SIEM via a collector. We'll share the exact schema.
[07:35] Marta: and SOC2 artifacts?
[07:40] Lena: yes, we'll attach our SOC2 cert and the controls mapping.
[07:48] (brief pause)
[08:00] Priya: ok next — network test results you mentioned earlier. can you run the experiment with same-AZ routing preference and report back?
[08:12] Marcus: yes we can run that. Proposed plan: 1) schedule runtime upgrade in staging (0.9.3), 2) flip routing to same-AZ preferred in staging, 3) run the 10k request benchmark (same script), 4) share spreadsheet with lat/throughput and raw traces.
[08:38] Ethan: timeline? we can't do downtime during biz hours.
[08:45] Marcus: upgrade is rolling and should be transparent; for safety we propose a maintenance window off-hours — Marcus proposes Saturday 02:00 UTC, ~1h. We'll coordinate.
[09:00] Priya: Saturday morning works for us, yes.
[09:08] Marcus: great. Also, note one more small note: we found a mis-configured health probe that in rare cases marked the local pod as unhealthy and routed traffic away. We patched the health probe logic on our side but we want to ensure your NLB health check aligns with the pod readiness.
[09:30] Sam: we'll check NLB thresholds and share sample config.
[09:38] Priya: regarding costs — if we prefer same-AZ that might reduce egress but could increase peak capacity cost. any estimate?
[09:50] Lena: we'll run a quick back-of-envelope after the benchmark; Marcus can attach a delta estimate in the post-run notes.
[10:02] Marta: on encryption at rest — are token logs redacted automatically? we need assurance that PII doesn't leak to logs.
[10:12] Marcus: token-level logs are redacted; we provide an option to redact more aggressively. We'll include config knobs in the security doc.
[10:25] (some typing)
[10:35] Lena: ok i want to recap before we wrap: Marcus will open the support ticket and propose two maintenance windows (one staging, one canary), we'll send SOC2/KMS docs by Tuesday (2026-03-31), Datafoundry to share traceroute/iptables export and NLB config, and after the staging upgrade we'll run the same benchmark and share the spreadsheet.
[10:55] Priya: sounds good. Marta — any other security blockers?
[11:02] Marta: just the SOC2 doc and KMS diagram; once we have that we'll re-run our internal checklist.
[11:12] Lena: perfect. Marcus anything else?
[11:18] Marcus: one more small ask — please enable packet capture on a single host during the staging run so we can correlate traces; only for 30m.
[11:28] Ethan: can do, we'll enable for the run.
[11:35] Priya: ok thanks everyone, good sync.
[11:38] (meeting ends)

References/Artifacts: shared folder: https://redwood.app/poc/datafoundry/benchmarks.xlsx, security pack link (to be attached), traceroutes/iptables dumps in shared folder.

Action items (auto): Marcus to open ticket for upgrade; Lena to send SOC2/KMS docs; Datafoundry to share network dumps and confirm windows.

Notes about transcript quality: medium — occasional mis-attribution and truncated filenames in uploads.
